svg.text: Where one output token's time goes · short prompt, concurrency 1
Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B · BF16 · 2 nodes × 8 MI300X · 8 × 400 Gb/s InfiniBand per node = 400 GB/s · GPU Direct RDMA off
A · Measured time per output token (ms) = 1000 ÷ median per-request decode speed
Light segment: up to TP8 × PP2's 11.9 ms; dark segment: the extra time per token, enlarged in panel B
B · The extra time per token, enlarged and drawn to scale with the time its InfiniBand data needs at 400 GB/s
Yellow sliver: moving its 11.4 MB per token at 400 GB/s takes 28 µs, 0.6% of the extra time
126 stripes = about 126 cross-node collectives per token (estimate: 62 layers × 2 all-reduces, plus 2 for the embedding and output layers). TP8 × PP2 performs as
many, inside a node; a cross-node one costs at least 35 µs more on average, while its ≈90 KB of data needs 0.23 µs on the wire
Yellow sliver: moving its 4.0 MB per token at 400 GB/s takes 10 µs, 0.2% of the extra time
Less data than TP16, yet more extra time. Not divided into all-reduces: the page's AMD note says the Triton expert kernels are slower with expert parallelism

Measured: time per token from the median per-request decode speed; InfiniBand receive from one-second samples inside the measured rounds, busier node, prompt share included. Estimated, not measured: the collective

count, read from the vLLM source (62 layers × 2 all-reduces, plus 2), and the extra cost per call, a lower bound assuming TP16's computation outside synchronization is no longer than TP8 × PP2's (at concurrency 1 a token
passes through all 62 layers in both, and TP16 halves each layer's sharded work).
